text:
anya: Heads-up, saw a 18-25% tail-latency regression on the 8-GPU TP+PP checkpoint after we flipped default to LL128+PROTO yesterday. Same model, same batch sizes.

kevin: ugh. Is it steady or spikey? any diffs in all-reduce time?

anya: steady when under load. overall throughput similar but p99 tokens up. perf-bot posted a quick breakdown: total token time +22%, allreduce time +48% on some ranks.

perf-bot: 
```
Summary: baseline (LL/nccl-algo=ring): p50=28ms p95=46ms p99=82ms
LL128+PROTO: p50=29ms p95=55ms p99=101ms
Allreduce avg per-step: baseline=1.8ms LL128=2.7ms
Affected ranks: [2,5,6] (higher skew)
```

sam: can you paste the kernel selector logs? maybe we picked a slower reduce kernel for small messages. I remember a proto path that increases fragments for small collective sizes.

anya: attaching excerpt from runtime log (snippet):
```
[2026-02-18 09:12:10] kernel_selector: chosen path=LL128_PROTO_FRAGMENTED, fragments=4, chunk_bytes=65536
[2026-02-18 09:12:10] nccl: using channel_map=0, channels=4, algo=PROTO, syncpoint=true
```

olivia: hmm fragments=4 seems high for our small msg sizes. Could be extra syncpoints introduced by proto fallback. Did we change channel packing?

kevin: iirc LL128 with PROTO sometimes splits and does extra synchronous copies when message < threshold. need nvprof or trace to confirm.

anya: uploaded trace: `trace-2143654321-anya.sq` — short highlights below.
```
Trace highlight: rank2 step 102: comm stall 5.6ms waiting on syncpoint, compute 0.3ms.
rank0 step 102: comm 1.9ms compute 1.7ms.
Interceptor shows imbalance in chunk counts across ranks (2 vs 5 chunks).
```

sam: that chunk imbalance smells like non-deterministic segmentation of tensors across TP/PP boundaries. Are we reordering chunks by size? recent kernel-selector change did an aggressive heuristic: sort by estimated latency -> pack smaller fragments last. Could put more work on particular ranks.

olivia: good call. Also check KV-cache warmup pattern — we've seen small prefix lengths produce tiny allreduces that get fragmented aggressively. If LL128+PROTO increases fragment count, overhead grows nonlinearly.

kevin: repro plan: 1) run single-step synthetic allreduce with sizes from 8KB..256KB to map fragment thresholds 2) run full workload with `NCCL_TOPO_DUMP=1` + `NCCL_PROTO=ALL/LL/LL128` 3) compare kernels selected and channel assignment logs.

anya: running 1 now, quick results:
```
8KB -> fragments=1 proto=LL, time=0.45ms
32KB -> fragments=2 proto=PROTO, time=1.9ms
64KB -> fragments=4 proto=PROTO, time=3.1ms
```

olivia: confirms threshold at ~24-30KB. Our internal kv message mix has many 32KB-ish messages (kvprefetch + prompt metadata). That explains spike.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) bump proto fragment threshold to 48KB 2) force channel packing to balance chunk counts 3) fallback to LL for small messages until kv batching changes.

kevin: which is lowest-risk? changing threshold seems simple but could hurt very large allreduces. forcing channel packing needs careful testing. fallback to LL for <48KB might be safest short-term.

anya: +1 on short-term fallback. I'll open a canary with `NCCL_PROTO=LL,LL128:>=48KB` and run 24h perf stove.

ci-bot: triggered job `eng-runtime/nccl-canary/2143654321` — canary started on 8 nodes with mixed traffic. Link: https://ci/2143654321

olivia: also let's file an issue to revisit kernel-selector heuristics — the sort-by-latency packing seems to produce skew under heterogenous per-rank message sizes. I'll add trace with chunk distribution viz in the ticket.

anya: creating issue now and attaching traces. Thanks all, will report back after canary finishes. :thumbsup:
